rows.subtype: Hopeful and apprehensive about the future [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult facing exams, placements or a move feels hope and dread. Planning, talking to mentors and small steps convert vague dread into manageable action.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, hope

rows.description: A young adult celebrating a success acknowledges help and effort, and avoids putting others down. Shared pride strengthens bonds, and public boasting can create distance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Bored and tired in study life [Expressing]
rows.description: A young adult in a dull lecture or overloaded semester shows yawns, doodling and phone use. Boredom, tiredness and poor sleep overlap, and structure, breaks and rest help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult keeps reactions muted in interviews, family gatherings or with elders. Restraint shows respect in many cultures, yet constant suppression can be tiring.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.subtype: Bodily signs are not lie detectors [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult sees someone sweat, blush or tremble in a questioning situation and wonders about guilt. These reactions occur in innocent people as well, so they must never be treated as proof.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: guilt, curiosity, awe

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.subtype: Trembling and sweating before high-stakes events [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult before viva, interview or speech feels shaky hands and damp palms from nerves. Preparation, grounding and reframing arousal as readiness help, and persistent panic deserves professional support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Direct versus indirect communication across cultures [Mismatch]
rows.description: A young adult meets people who state needs plainly and others who hint through politeness or silence. Neither is better, and adaptable listeners ask clarifying questions kindly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult carrying stress for weeks shows it in tired face, short answers or constant irritability. Long-lasting displays call for rest, support and sometimes professional help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult keeps a flat face on results day or during a proposal, feeling great excitement or fear inside. A blank face shows control rather than absence of feeling, so others should not assume indifference.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, excitement

rows.subtype: Speaking politely while angry in formal settings [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult in an interview, service dispute or family setting stays courteous while frustrated. Composure is useful, though the anger needs a healthy outlet, and a calm firm request protects boundaries.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
